q1.question: What should I do when a column has blank values?

hits.text: A NOT_NULL rule says a column must have a value in every row. It takes no parameters. A blank cell counts as a failure. This rule fits columns such as a student ID, where a missing value makes the whole row useless to the team that receives the file. When a NOT_NULL rule fails, DataPact records how many rows were blank. The usual causes are a broken export or a new optional field in the source system. The owner of the dataset should ask the source team whether the blanks are expected before changing the contract.

An ALLOWED_VALUES rule lists every value a column may hold. The parameters hold the list. A status column might allow ACTIVE, INACTIVE and AUDIT. A new code in the file fails the rule even if it is valid in the source system, so this rule is the one most often changed when a source team adds a status.

A RANGE rule says a number must fall between a minimum and a maximum. The parameters hold those two limits. A credit hours column might use a range of 0 to 24. Values outside the limits are counted as violations, and sample values are kept for the person who reviews the run.

q2.question: Why would a key column have duplicate values?

hits.text: A UNIQUE rule says no value may appear twice in a column. It takes no parameters. It is the rule to use for keys such as an order number. A failed UNIQUE rule usually means the file was exported twice or two batches were joined together. Duplicates can also come from a legitimate change. If a student can now hold two enrollments in one term, the key is no longer the student ID alone. In that case the contract should change, and the change should be saved as a new contract version.

q3.question: Can I edit a contract that was already used?

hits.text: A contract is the written agreement about what the files of a dataset must contain. Each contract belongs to one dataset and holds a list of rules. A contract that has been used in a validation run must never be edited. Any change is saved as a new version, so old runs can still be read against the rules they were checked with.

A violation stores the rule that failed, the number of failed rows and a few sample values. A person then records what the failure meant. The resolution says whether the data was wrong or the contract was out of date. Keeping this decision matters because the same violation may come back in a later file, and the team can see how it was handled last time.

q4.question: When does a validation run count as failed?

hits.text: A validation run is one occasion on which an uploaded file was checked against one contract version. The run records the file, the contract version and the outcome. A run passes when every rule passes. A run fails when at least one rule fails, and each failed rule produces one aggregated violation rather than one record per bad row.
